title: Coercion Forecast
summary: Predict what R prints when types mix, logicals are added up and NAs appear.
hints: A vector holds one type. The order is logical → numeric → character: R moves everything to the most flexible type present.
Any calculation with `NA` in it gives `NA` unless you ask R to skip missing values.

choices: Error: a vector can't mix types
quiz.explain: One character value makes the whole vector character, so `1` becomes `"1"` and `TRUE` becomes `"TRUE"`. The quotes in the output are the giveaway.

quiz.prompt: No text this time. What does R print?
quiz.explain: Numeric is more flexible than logical, so the logicals become numbers: `TRUE` is 1 and `FALSE` is 0.

quiz.prompt: Four pilots answered a yes/no item. What does R print?
quiz.code:
passed <- c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE)
sum(passed)
mean(passed)
quiz.explain: `sum()` of a logical vector **counts** the `TRUE`s and `mean()` gives the **proportion** that are `TRUE`. You'll use this all the time: `mean(scores > 50)` is the proportion above 50.

quiz.prompt: A column of ages was typed with one word in it. What does R print?
choices:
Warning: NAs introduced by coercion
[1] 24 NA 31
quiz.explain: R can't turn `"twenty"` into a number, so it becomes `NA` and R **warns** you. That warning is how you find typing errors after an import.

quiz.prompt: One score is missing. What does R print?
quiz.code:
scores <- c(12, NA, 18)
mean(scores)
mean(scores, na.rm = TRUE)
quiz.explain: `NA` means "unknown", so a mean that includes it is unknown too. `na.rm = TRUE` drops the missing value first and averages the two that remain: (12 + 18) / 2 = 15. SPSS drops missing values for you; R makes you say so.
